title: Routing Compatibility Adaptor & Safety Layer for DSL Schemas
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Goal: introduce a compatibility adaptor and runtime safety layer that allows new routing DSL schema extensions to be validated and enforced while preserving backward compatibility for existing customer configs. This ticket covers: (1) an adaptor that rewrites deprecated/legacy rule forms to the canonical policy shape at read-time, (2) a staged validation pipeline that supports lenient and strict modes, (3) a runtime safety harness that prevents unsafe routing actions (e.g., cross-region routing for data-restricted tenants), and (4) integration tests and telemetry for gradual rollout.
comments: 2026-02-11 - Kickoff: Drafted the adaptor design and compatibility table. Decided adaptor will run in the control plane at config ingestion to avoid per-request overhead. - Aisha

2026-02-13 - Trade-offs: We discussed doing a full transpiler vs a lightweight adaptor. Chosen lightweight adaptor to minimize surface area and make rollbacks easier; full transpiler deferred to later if we need aggressive optimizations. - Marco

2026-02-15 - Review feedback from Infra: Ensure adaptor has deterministic idempotent transforms and emits a canonical hash for config diffing. Also add a safety flag so Dedicated customers can opt into strict validation. - Priya (Infra)

2026-02-17 - Implementation note: Added a read-time transformation hook in the policy loader. Hook stages: parse -> transform -> staged-validate -> emit canonical JSON + validation report. Partial implementation in branch gh/redwood-inference/policy-adaptor/merge-request-7890. - Marco

2026-02-19 - QA plan updated: Add routing simulator scenarios for region selection churn, tiered fallbacks, and forced-model-variant-mismatch; validate metrics for misroute_count, fallback_rate, and config_reject_rate. Also added property tests for round-trip transform correctness. - QA Team
acceptance_criteria: Adaptor correctly normalizes at least three legacy DSL variants into canonical rules (examples in confluence doc)
Staged validation supports lenient (warn) and strict (reject) modes and is toggleable per-customer
Runtime safety harness blocks at least two classes of unsafe actions and surfaces clear audit logs
Integration tests (simulator) show <0.5% additional routing latency at 95th percentile in canary
Telemetry dashboards show proper routing error metrics and a roll-forward/rollback runbook is documented
